dimensionScores.evidence: File present at packages/llm-http-proxy/src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts and contains both required imports: `import { Interceptor } from './interceptor';` and `import type { LlmLogEntry } from './options';`.

Literal describe.skip criterion does not apply due to contract shift — the new design is a DEFAULT suite (verified npm test shows +1 test passing, not skipped), but the SPIRIT is BETTER satisfied: zero external network egress (127.0.0.1-only with no credentials, no DNS lookup, no public-DNS dependency).

Test fires exactly one `https.request` POST against the local HTTPS server, awaits two `setImmediate` ticks, and asserts `entries.length===1`, `entries[0].url` contains '127.0.0.1', `typeof entries[0].model === 'string'`, and `JSON.stringify(entries[0]).length > 0` — the SPIRIT (real HTTPS interception + entry-shape assertions) is fully met, just with localhost instead of example.com.

File contains zero *_API_KEY reads; the only env var touched is `process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` (a TLS-validation switch, not a credential); header comment explicitly states the suite needs no API key or network access.

Interceptor built with `providers: [/127\.0\.0\.1|localhost/]` and a logger pushing into local array, `interceptor.install()` before the request, and a `try/finally` that calls `interceptor.restore()` BEFORE the outer finally that closes the server, removes the temp cert dir, and restores the prior NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED value.

Header comment (lines 1-11) explains the localhost-only rationale, deterministic/CI behavior, and absence of credentials; the two setImmediate awaits are present in code — SPIRIT (documentation + flush pattern) met, though the comment does not explicitly call out the two-setImmediate flush rule since the file is no longer opt-in under the shifted contract.

phases.notes: CONTRACT SHIFT from original rubric: phase was originally planned as an opt-in suite gated on npm_lifecycle_event firing one real fetch to https://example.com. After sandbox network-isolation blocked verification, the user redesigned the suite to use a localhost-only HTTPS round-trip (openssl-generated self-signed cert + node:https createServer on 127.0.0.1) and run by default with no opt-in gate. This shifts the rubric's 'default-npm-test-skips-suite' and 'opt-in-and-flush-documentation' dimensions from literal-applicable to spirit-applicable: the new design achieves a strictly stronger property (zero external network egress, not just credential-free public fetch). All 6 dimensions pass under re-grade; phase marked done. The other 3 phases (anthropic/openai/gemini) remain unchanged — they still gate on API-key presence per their spec because they MUST hit external provider APIs.

phases.notes:
Phase implemented as a default-skipping suite that resolves to describe.skip under both `npm test` and direct `npx jest src/anthropic.integration.test.ts` (no key set) and would run one real https.request POST under ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<real-key> npx jest src/anthropic.integration.test.ts. The live path was NOT executed in this session (no key set in the orchestrator env), so the live-call behavior is unverified by execution — only the skip path is empirically proven; the run-path assertions are validated by code-reading against the rubric. Pattern mirrors fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts (try/finally install/restore) and benchmark.test.ts (if/else describe|describe.skip gate). Empty-string env var treated as unset for ALL three env vars (apiKey, baseUrl, model — explicit length checks). Used done-callback test pattern with nested setImmediate for flush (cannot await inside a done-callback). Defense-in-depth negative assertion guards apiKey leakage across any future redaction regression. No new exports added to src/index.ts (test-only file).

CONTRACT EXTENSION (post-grade, user request): added ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_MODEL env overrides following the same env-var pattern as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Defaults match the rubric's documented minimums (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022), so all 6 rubric dimensions still pass unchanged against the default path. The interceptor's providers filter is now derived from new URL(parsedUrl).hostname so a custom baseUrl still routes captured requests correctly; the URL assertion now compares against `${parsedUrl.hostname}${parsedUrl.pathname}` so it stays correct for any baseUrl. The model assertion still uses the 'claude' substring (this is the anthropic integration test — non-Claude models are out of scope). Gates re-run after extension: typecheck exit 0, lint 0 errors (only pre-existing otel warnings), npm test 127 passed + 3 skipped, direct jest skip path unchanged (1 skipped), build exit 0. Re-grade was NOT performed because defaults match the rubric's documented values — the extension is purely additive flexibility and does not weaken any rubric dimension.
